title: A bill to require the Securities and Exchange Commission to issue rules relating to the use of artificial intelligence by public companies, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: This bill requires the Securities and Exchange Commission to create rules that govern how public companies can use artificial intelligence. It also includes additional provisions related to AI and other regulatory objectives.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is designed to make sure that AI research is safe, reliable, and trustworthy. It establishes federal rules, oversight committees, and penalties to ensure AI projects follow high safety standards and that their results can be clearly understood and replicated by others.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to set up a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to defend critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It aims to test AI tools and processes that can help protect essential services such as energy, water, and communications.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force dedicated to protecting and securing AI systems that are critical to national security and infrastructure. It aims to develop guidelines, best practices, and oversight mechanisms to reduce risks associated with AI technologies.

title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency a pilot program to be known as the "BRIDGE AI Mission Program" to recruit and manage artificial intelligence and emerging technology professionals on a temporary basis to support the core mission of the Agency, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This proposal amends the 2002 Homeland Security Act to create a pilot program within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency called the BRIDGE AI Mission Program. The program will recruit and manage temporary AI and emerging technology professionals to support the agency's core missions.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed regulation that seeks to set comprehensive rules for the design, use, and governance of artificial intelligence systems. It aims to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability while encouraging innovation and protecting citizens' rights.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 is designed to stop companies from using automated software to secretly coordinate prices or market strategies. It sets up rules, monitoring, and penalties to ensure algorithms do not undermine fair competition in the marketplace.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 is a bill that aims to help small businesses develop and implement AI solutions by providing training, resources, and support. It seeks to close the AI skills gap and boost competitiveness for small businesses in a rapidly evolving digital economy.

title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency the National Cyber and AI Investigations Board to investigate significant cyber incidents, cyber incidents involving terrorism, and cyber incidents involving artificial intelligence, to determine root causes and develop recommendations to prevent similar incidents and address terrorism threats to the United States, including threats relating to the malicious use of information systems or artificial intelligence by covered foreign adversaries, including terrorist organizations, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The bill would create a new National Cyber and AI Investigations Board inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. This board would investigate major cyber incidents—including those involving terrorism or artificial intelligence—to identify root causes and recommend ways to prevent similar attacks, especially from foreign adversaries or terrorist groups.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a proposed law that would temporarily pause the building and operation of new AI data centers. It aims to address concerns about environmental impact, energy usage, and data privacy while regulators review and set new standards for AI infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to curb the environmental footprint of AI systems by mandating that developers assess, report, and minimize energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, and resource usage. The act also sets up regulatory oversight and incentives to encourage the adoption of greener AI technologies and practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction and operation of data centers that support AI technology. This pause is intended to give regulators time to review the environmental, security, and societal impacts of AI‑driven data infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is designed to reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies by setting standards for energy use, carbon emissions, and resource efficiency. It encourages companies to adopt greener practices throughout the AI development and deployment lifecycle.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a proposed U.S. law that aims to regulate the development and deployment of artificial intelligence to protect national security, privacy, and public safety. It seeks to establish oversight mechanisms, safety standards, and accountability measures for AI systems used within the United States.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes sector‑specific regulations to manage the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence technologies. It sets standards for safety, transparency, and accountability, tailoring requirements to the unique risks and benefits of each industry such as healthcare, finance, and transportation.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This law aims to stop AI companies from inflating prices and using AI to set or manipulate wages unfairly. It creates rules and enforcement mechanisms to ensure fair pricing and prevent wage fixing in AI-driven labor markets.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress must refuse to give additional money or special regulatory help to companies or financial institutions that are at risk of insolvency due to stress in the AI market. Instead, Congress should focus on providing support to all Americans who have been harmed by these situations.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a regulatory framework that governs the use of AI within the veterinary sector, ensuring tools meet safety, transparency, and accountability standards. It aims to protect animal welfare and promote responsible AI deployment in veterinary practices.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 requires that all medical diagnoses, treatment plans, and patient counseling be performed by licensed physicians rather than artificial intelligence systems. It establishes penalties for unauthorized AI use in clinical settings to protect patient safety and uphold professional medical standards.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies that use automated decision‑making systems to assess the potential for bias and document how those algorithms affect protected groups. The bill aims to increase transparency and accountability for AI systems in both public and private sectors, ensuring they meet fairness and safety standards.
